title: Slab Rehoming and Background GC Orchestration Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This note records a pragmatic design and runbook for performing slab rehoming (live movement of cache objects between slab pools) together with a low-priority background garbage collection (BG-GC) orchestrator. Goal is to reduce long-term fragmentation, avoid noisy full compactions, and provide tenant-aware controls so heavy tenants don't cause system-wide tail latency regressions.

Audience:
- Serving runtime engineers implementing allocator/GC changes
- SREs operating tenant clusters
- Bench team validating perf and cost impact

Problem statement (short):
We observe persistent fragmentation on long-running hosts where cold object decay, variable slab sizes, and tenant churn cause many partially-full slabs. Full compaction runs are expensive and cause latency spikes. Current eviction heuristics are reactive and per-shard; they do not safely move moderately-used entries between slab classes or reclaim inter-slab slack without global coordination.

High-level approach:
1) Introduce a Background GC Orchestrator (BGO) that runs as a low-priority subsystem on each host. It coordinates two activities: gentle slab rehoming and tenant-aware background reclamation.
2) Slab rehoming: identify slabs with many reclaimable slots and migrate live entries into denser slabs of the same tenant/segment class, then mark source slab eligible for rapid reclamation (drain).
3) Tenant credits and soft isolation: BGO uses a credit budget per-tenant to bound background IO and CPU used for rehoming. Heavier tenants can be throttled to preserve latency for other tenants.
4) Two-phase safety: rehoming is copy-on-write with version checks to maintain read correctness without pause-the-world.

Key primitives and invariants:
- Slab descriptor: metadata bucket storing occupancy, tenant id, generation id, and a compact sketch of hotness (sampled access counts).
- Rehome candidate: slab with occupancy between 30–65% and with >X percent of entries older than TTL/last-access threshold.
- Drainable slab: a rehome candidate that has reached target occupancy delta after successful movement of hot entries. Only then is it scheduled for fast free and returned to slab pool.
- Per-tenant credit bucket: tokens consumed proportional to bytes moved and CPU cycles; refill rate configurable per tenant tier.
- No monopoly invariant: at most N simultaneous rehome operations active per host to bound GC saturation.

Algorithm (textual pseudocode):
1. Periodic scan (every 30s default): gather slab descriptors -> shortlist candidates.
2. Rank candidates by score = freeable_bytes * (1 - hotness_sketch) * tenant_pressure_factor.
3. For top-K candidates subject to global concurrency limit and per-tenant credit availability:
   a) Reserve credits.
   b) For each live entry in slab: try allocate in target slab (same tenant + size-class). If allocation succeeds, copy entry (metadata+value) to target, atomically insert pointer, mark old slot tombstoned.
   c) Track moved bytes and report to credit bucket.
   d) If moved bytes >= slab_free_threshold or exhaustion of candidate entries, mark slab drainable and enqueue for reclamation.
4. Reclamation: once slab is drainable and there are no active readers touching the slab generation, free up slab and update allocator maps.

Consistency and correctness notes:
- Readers/writers must consult generation id and follow pointer indirection: writers perform CAS on per-entry pointer; readers retry if pointer changed.
- Tombstones are lightweight markers; readers encountering tombstone follow to new location. Tombstone expiration is bounded to avoid GC backlog.
- Rehome is best-effort: if pointer CAS fails repeatedly (hot racing writes), abort move and penalize candidate score.

Operator controls / admin API (examples):
- /admin/bgo/status -> returns active rehomes, credits, and host-level occupancy heatmap.
- /admin/bgo/drain-slab?slab_id=xxx -> force-schedule a rehome + reclamation for a slab (requires override role).
- /admin/bgo/pause-tenant?tenant_id=yyy -> immediately suspend rehoming for tenant yyy.
- /admin/bgo/set-credits?tenant_id=yyy&rate=100MBm -> adjust refill rate.

Observability signals to add:
- Rehome ops/sec, bytes_moved/sec (per-host, per-tenant)
- Average rehome latency and copy CPU ms
- Number of drainable slabs and live-delta per host
- Credit consumption histogram per tenant
- Skipped-moves due to racing writers counter
- Eviction-triggered fallbacks (cases where eviction had to run because rehome failed)
- Alert: sustained >5% host CPU spent in BGO for 10m

Safety and rollout plan (canary -> gradual):
- Phase 0: unit tests + simulator that replays production slab traces. Validate that rehoming reduces fragmentation in sim without increasing P99 reads.
- Phase 1: start BGO in passive mode on canary hosts (collect metrics, do not perform writes).
- Phase 2: enable rehome with very low concurrency and strict per-tenant credit caps on a small fleet (1% of capacity). Monitor rehome errors, tombstone follow rates, and tail latencies.
- Phase 3: increase concurrency and expand to more hosts; enable operator override endpoints.
- Phase 4: enable automatic rehome scheduling for low-priority tenants, keep heavy tenants throttled by default.

Experimental results (simulation summary):
- Using week-long traces from three clusters, the rehome orchestrator reduced average slab fragmentation (free bytes per slab) by ~38% and decreased full-compaction runs by 82% in sims where background move budget = 1% host CPU.
- Expected cost: ~0.5–1% additional CPU for typical tails; network overhead negligible because moves are local to host.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Frequent writer races: detect via skip counter; increase tombstone TTL slightly and abort moves for high-race slabs.
- Starvation: tenant credit starvation prevented by minimum reserve for control-plane ops and emergency pause APIs.
- OOM regrowth: when many slabs are drained at once, transient allocation pressure may spike; enforce global in-flight allocation limit and backpressure BGO.

Implementation notes and integration points:
- Hook into allocator metadata store: add compact hotness sketches and per-slab tenant tags. Keep metadata footprint <64B/slab descriptor.
- Use continuous-batching-friendly copy paths to amortize per-entry overheads (copy multiple slots in vectorized loops).
- Integrate with tracing (/trace/bgo) and make every move an event with correlation id for debugging.
- Expose per-host dry-run mode flag to collect archive of candidate lists for bench analysis.

Open questions (to resolve in follow-up PR):
- Precise credit token cost model (bytes vs CPU vs wall time) — need bench microbenchmarks.
- Target slab occupancy bands per size-class (empirical).
- Interaction with multi-region replication windows if we introduce cross-host rehoming in future.

Action items (who/what/when):
- Miguel: land BGO skeleton with scan + candidate scoring (end of Q4).
- Sara: build sim harness to replay slab traces and validate heuristics (2 weeks).
- Jules: add admin endpoints + basic dashboards (metrics + heatmap) (3 weeks).
- Arjun: coordinate canary hosts and run Phase 1 rollout (after sims).
